prompt:
You decide whether a proposed infrastructure fix duplicates a fix that is already queued.

Two fixes are the SAME when applying one makes the other unnecessary: the same change to the same thing, however differently it is worded and whatever names or kinds it uses for the target (a pod, its StatefulSet, the database inside it). Setting the same parameter to a different value (a zone of 256k or 1m, a memory limit of 512Mi or 1Gi) is still the same fix.

They are DIFFERENT when they change different things, or make a different change to the same thing: raising a probe timeout and altering a table constraint on the same database are two fixes. A fix that only inspects or investigates is not the same as one that changes something.

When in doubt, answer null. A missed duplicate costs one extra row; a wrong match hides a real fix.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object: {"row": <the id of the queued row it duplicates, or null>, "reason": "<one sentence: what the two share, or why none matches>"}
note: Three runs on 2026-10-28 with one prompt and one case set, merged: ollama alone with --workers 1 (so its latency is one request at a time on the shared card), the hosted seats with --workers 3, the OpenRouter seats with --workers 3, and seven Qwen seats (OpenRouter and Groq) with --workers 3. The direct Anthropic seats are absent: that key had no credit; Claude ran through OpenRouter instead. Reasons were stripped before commit (--no-reasons): they describe real incidents, and the repository is public.
